moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
learningObjectives: Describe the business benefit of using portals.
Identify the elements of a portal.
Update a portal with new landing pages.
Change the styling of a control at runtime.
Identify the attributes used to dynamically display information.

elements.description: A portal is the user's workspace — the overall interface a user sees when they log in. Tailoring portals by CHANNEL and PERSONA lets each type of user perform their job efficiently with the right tools and information front-and-center.

Portals deliver a role-appropriate, branded, productive experience: each Persona gets a workspace suited to their tasks, improving efficiency and the user experience while keeping branding consistent.
A portal is composed of regions such as a HEADER (logo, search, utilities), NAVIGATION (menu to move between areas), and LANDING PAGES / dashboards that present content and work in the main area.

Landing pages are configurable pages within a portal (e.g., dashboards, reports, custom content). You can UPDATE a portal by adding new landing pages and corresponding navigation entries so users reach the information they need.

elements.text: A portal is a customized cockpit: the header is the dashboard frame, the navigation is the control panel, and landing pages are the gauges/screens. Each role (pilot vs. engineer) gets a cockpit laid out for their job.

bulletPoints: Portals are tailored by channel and Persona so users work efficiently.
Portal regions: header, navigation, and landing pages/dashboards.
Update a portal by adding new landing pages and navigation links.

elements.description: Style formats and conditional formatting change how a control is displayed at run time — for example, highlighting overdue values — without altering the underlying field value.
Styling affects only how information is DISPLAYED; it does not change the stored value. This keeps branding/appearance consistent while the data model stays intact.

elements.text: Styling a control is like highlighting text in a document: the words (data) are unchanged, but the highlight (style) draws the reader's eye to what matters.

bulletPoints: Apply style formats/conditional formatting to controls to improve appearance and draw attention.
Styling changes presentation only — the underlying field value is unchanged.

elements.description: You can control the VISIBILITY of fields and UI elements dynamically — showing or hiding them based on conditions (for example, show the 'Reason for rejection' field only when the decision is 'Rejected'). This tailors the View to the context.

elements.term: Attributes used to dynamically display information
elements.description: Visibility and dynamic behavior are driven by conditions/attributes such as 'visible when' a condition (When rule) is true, or comparisons against field values — so the UI adapts to the data and the user's situation in real time.

elements.text: Dynamic visibility is a smart form that reveals follow-up questions only when relevant: tick 'Other' and a text box appears; otherwise it stays hidden — the form adapts to your answers.

bulletPoints: Use visibility conditions (visible-when) to show/hide fields based on data or context.
Dynamic display is driven by conditions/When rules comparing field values.
Dynamic UI keeps Views relevant and uncluttered for each situation and Persona.

examPitfalls.title: Portal purpose: tailored by channel and Persona
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Portals exist to give each Persona/channel a role-appropriate, efficient workspace — not a one-size-fits-all screen.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Match the portal to the Persona/channel so each user sees the tools and information they need.

examPitfalls.title: Elements of a portal
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Know the portal regions: header, navigation, and landing pages/dashboards.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If asked to identify portal elements, recall header + navigation + landing pages.

examPitfalls.title: Updating a portal = adding landing pages
examPitfalls.trapDescription: You extend a portal by adding new landing pages (and navigation entries), not by altering the data model.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Add landing pages + navigation links to surface new content in a portal.

examPitfalls.title: Styling changes presentation, not data
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Changing a control's style at runtime affects display only; the stored value is unchanged.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use style formats/conditional formatting for appearance; data stays the same.

examPitfalls.title: Dynamic visibility uses conditions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Show/hide behavior is driven by visibility conditions (visible-when / When rules) comparing field values.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: To show a field only in certain situations, set a visibility condition rather than duplicating Views.

examPitfalls.title: Customization improves efficiency
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The goal of UI customization is helping each user complete work efficiently with relevant, well-presented information.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Tie portal/landing-page/visibility choices to user productivity and clarity.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A company wants CSRs and managers to each log into a workspace tailored to their job, with the right tools front-and-center. What Pega feature delivers this?
practiceQuiz.hint: Portals provide each user role with a tailored workspace matching their Persona and channel needs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Portals provide role-appropriate workspaces tailored by Persona and channel so each user works efficiently in a relevant environment. The other features serve calculation, timing, and data-manipulation purposes, not workspace configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is configuring a portal for customer service representatives and wants to understand the main structural regions that make up a Pega portal. Which THREE of the following are elements or regions of a portal?
practiceQuiz.hint: A portal consists of a header/navigation frame, menu, and configurable landing pages or dashboards.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A portal comprises a header, navigation menu, and landing pages or dashboards. An Access Role is a security construct that defines permissions, not a region or component of a portal. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA needs to surface a new reporting dashboard inside an existing portal. What is the appropriate approach?

options.text: Add a new landing page (and a navigation entry) to the portal
Change the Case Type's Data Model

practiceQuiz.hint: Adding new landing pages and navigation entries extends a portal's content and reachability.
practiceQuiz.rationale: To update a portal, architects add new landing pages and configure navigation entries that link to them. Changes to the Data Model, Access Groups, or Wait Steps do not add portal content or navigation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA wants overdue amounts to appear in red and statuses to show as colored badges, without changing the stored values. What is this?

options.text: Changing the styling/presentation of a control at runtime (conditional formatting)
A Data Transform that edits the values

practiceQuiz.hint: Styling changes the appearance only — the underlying data value is never affected.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Applying style formats or conditional formatting changes how a control is displayed without altering the stored data value. Data Transforms change values; validation enforces rules; SLAs govern timing — none affect display styling.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The 'Reason for rejection' field should appear only when the decision is 'Rejected'. How should a BA configure this?

options.text: Set a visibility condition (visible-when the decision is Rejected)
Add a default value to the field

practiceQuiz.hint: Visibility conditions show or hide a UI element based on a When rule evaluating field values at run time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dynamic visibility uses a visible-when condition to show the field only when the decision is Rejected. Separate portals, defaults, and urgency don't conditionally show a field.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA changes the display control of a currency field from a text input to a slider for a better user experience. Does this styling change alter the field's underlying stored value?

options.text: No — styling affects presentation only; the stored value is unchanged
Only if the field is calculated

practiceQuiz.hint: Applying a style format to text changes only how it looks — the underlying value stays exactly as stored.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Styling changes only the visual presentation of data; the underlying value remains intact in all cases. Styling never overwrites, deletes, or transforms the stored field value under any condition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA wants certain fields on a View to appear only when a specific checkbox is checked by the user at runtime. What primarily drives this dynamic display behavior on a View?

options.text: Conditions/attributes such as visible-when (When rules) that compare field values
The number of operators logged in

practiceQuiz.hint: Dynamic UI visibility is driven by conditions — When rules — that evaluate field values at run time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dynamic display is driven by visibility conditions (visible-when / When rules) that evaluate field values at run time. Ruleset version numbers, login counts, and UI themes do not control individual field visibility.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is justifying the investment in Persona-specific portal customization to a cost-conscious project sponsor. What is the core business benefit of tailoring portals to Personas?

options.text: Each user gets a role-appropriate, efficient workspace, improving productivity and experience
It removes the need for Access Roles

practiceQuiz.hint: Tailored portals provide each Persona with an efficient, role-relevant workspace that improves productivity.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tailored portals give each Persona an efficient, contextually relevant workspace that boosts user productivity and experience. They do not replace security layers, delete data, or eliminate the need for validation rules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are valid ways to customize the UI for efficiency and branding?

options.text: Apply conditional styling so important values stand out
Use visibility conditions to show only relevant fields

practiceQuiz.hint: UI customization tools include control styling (appearance) and conditional visibility (show/hide logic).
practiceQuiz.rationale: Conditional styling and visibility conditions customize the UI for clarity and branding. Editing the database schema or deleting the Resolution Stage are not UI-customization techniques. No partial credit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is adding a new performance dashboard to the CSR portal in App Studio to extend what agents can see on login. Which statement about landing pages in a Pega portal is correct?

options.text: They are configurable pages within a portal (dashboards, reports, custom content) that you can add to update a portal
They are the same as Access Groups

practiceQuiz.hint: Landing pages are configurable content pages you add inside a portal to extend it with new sections.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Landing pages are configurable content pages within a portal that architects add to extend its available content and navigation. They are not Access Groups, permission sets, or data storage locations.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A field should be hidden for the customer Persona but visible for the manager Persona on the same View. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Use a visibility condition based on the user's Persona/role
Hard-delete the field from the Data Model

practiceQuiz.hint: A visibility condition referencing the user's role or Persona can show a field only to specific users.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A visibility condition referencing the current user's role or Persona makes a field visible only to users who match — for example, managers. Deleting the field removes it for all users; Wait Steps and SLAs serve workflow-timing purposes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is setting user experience design goals for a new customer service portal that will serve both agents and managers. Which TWO outcomes does effective UI customization primarily aim to achieve?

options.text: Users complete their work more efficiently with relevant information
Consistent branding and appearance across the application

practiceQuiz.hint: UI customization improves efficiency and branding consistency for each user role.
practiceQuiz.rationale: UI customization improves user efficiency by providing relevant, role-specific interfaces and keeps branding consistent across all portals. It does not bypass business-logic validation or eliminate the need for Persona-based access control. No partial credit.

quickRecap.value: The user's workspace, tailored by Persona/channel for efficiency and consistent branding.
Configurable content pages within a portal; add new ones (with navigation) to update a portal.
Change presentation at runtime (style formats/conditional formatting); affects display only, not the stored value.
Show/hide fields via visibility conditions (visible-when / When rules) comparing field values, adapting the View to context/Persona.
